concerns.text: All tasks are marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but the plan defines strict producer‑consumer ordering (e.g., T001 must finish before T002, T002 before T003, etc.). This violates the `[P]` contract which requires true parallel safety with no hidden shared state or ordering requirement.
Task T004 depends on the output of T003, yet it is also marked `[P]`. The `[P]` tag is inappropriate because the split generation cannot run safely in parallel with latent generation.
Tasks T005 and T006 (model training) are sequentially dependent on the split files and latent data, but both carry the `[P]` tag, which incorrectly signals they can be executed concurrently.
Task T007 (ablation) consumes the distilled model checkpoints produced by T005; marking it `[P]` creates a false parallel‑safety claim.
Task T008 (downstream evaluation) requires both distilled and baseline checkpoints; the `[P]` tag is misleading because it must wait for T005 and T006 to complete.
Task T009 (fallback intrinsic evaluation) depends on the existence of downstream results or latent metrics; it should not be marked `[P]`.
Task T010 (checksum & state logging) aggregates hashes of all generated artifacts; it must run after every other task, so the `[P]` tag is invalid.
Task T011 (end‑to‑end pipeline smoke test) invokes the full workflow; it cannot be parallel‑safe with any preceding tasks and should not carry the `[P]` tag.
